name: ScanDeath
author: burncycle

sections.description:
ScanDeath helps protect WordPress against suspicious and malicious requests.

The plugin works without a paid account or external service. Local protection is available immediately after activation.

Main features:

  • Local request protection with bundled security rules.
  • Temporary IP blocking with automatic release after the configured block time.
  • Security event logging.
  • Safe, Balanced, and Aggressive protection modes.
  • Trusted IP addresses.
  • Optional ScanDeath Cloud rule synchronization.
  • Optional advisory IP reputation information.
  • Local advisory risk scoring for suspicious events.
  • Support for Apache-compatible servers and WordPress/PHP protection behind Nginx.
  • Country- and site-specific date/time display based on the WordPress settings.
  • Admin-menu counter showing the number of currently blocked IP addresses.

Optional ScanDeath Cloud service

ScanDeath can optionally synchronize additional security rules from the ScanDeath Cloud service.

A ScanDeath Cloud service key is only used to authenticate the optional external service. It does not unlock or enable local plugin features.

Automatic Cloud synchronization is disabled until a valid service key is configured.

Hosted service information:
* Terms of Use: https://scandeath.com/terms/
* Privacy Policy: https://scandeath.com/privacy/

The Cloud service returns rule data only. The plugin does not download or execute PHP, JavaScript, or other executable code from the service.

Optional IP reputation checks

The Blocked IPs and Logs pages can display advisory information from public threat and reputation sources.

Administrators may also enable Proxycheck and AbuseIPDB checks under ScanDeath > Settings. These checks are disabled by default.

When enabled, the visitor IP address being checked is sent to the selected provider. AbuseIPDB requires its own API key. Proxycheck can be used with limited keyless requests or with a separate API key.

Reputation information is advisory only. It does not automatically block, unblock, or whitelist an IP address.

Usage

Use ScanDeath > Dashboard to view the current protection status and synchronize optional Cloud rules.

Use ScanDeath > Blocked IPs to view currently blocked addresses.

Use ScanDeath > Logs to review recorded security events.

Use ScanDeath > Settings to configure protection mode, block duration, trusted IPs, Cloud synchronization, and optional reputation services.

Privacy

Without optional external services, ScanDeath keeps its security processing on the WordPress site.

Local event logs may contain visitor IP addresses because IP addresses are required for IP blocking and security analysis. The log-retention period can be configured in ScanDeath settings.

If ScanDeath Cloud is configured, rule synchronization sends the site URL, plugin version, and Cloud service key to the configured Cloud service. Individual visitor logs and blocked IP addresses are not sent as part of Cloud rule synchronization.

If optional Proxycheck or AbuseIPDB checks are enabled, the IP address being checked is sent to the selected provider.

Please review the privacy policies of any external services you enable.

Help & Support

Open ScanDeath > Help in the WordPress administration area for setup information and links to documentation.

Website: https://scandeath.com/
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, open Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Upload the ScanDeath ZIP file.
  3. Activate ScanDeath.
  4. Open ScanDeath > Dashboard.
  5. Local protection is active immediately.
  6. Optional: configure ScanDeath Cloud or IP reputation services under ScanDeath > Settings.
sections.faq:
Does ScanDeath require a paid account?

No. Local protection works without an external account or service.

What is the ScanDeath Cloud service key for?

It authenticates the optional ScanDeath Cloud service. It does not unlock local plugin functionality.

How long is an IP blocked?

The default block duration is 10 minutes. You can change the duration in the ScanDeath settings.

What happens when a blocked IP expires?

The block is removed automatically when the IP accesses the site again after the configured block period has ended.

Can I trust an IP address so it is not blocked?

Yes. Add trusted addresses under ScanDeath > Settings.

Does ScanDeath work with Nginx?

Yes. ScanDeath protects requests that pass through WordPress/PHP. Static files or cached responses served without WordPress are outside the plugin’s control and should be protected by the web server or another firewall if required.

What can I do if I accidentally block myself?

Use the emergency-off option described in ScanDeath > Help or access the site from a trusted administrator connection and adjust the trusted IP settings.

What happens when I uninstall ScanDeath?

Deleting ScanDeath through WordPress removes its local settings, rules, logs, blocked-IP data, caches, and scheduled tasks. A normal deactivation or update does not delete this data.
